full_text_en:
Zhao Hengdong Acquitted and Released

Defendant: Zhao Hengdong, male, 47 years old, engineer at the Academic Office of Shenyang Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, concurrently Deputy Secretary-General of the Liaoning Provincial Computer Society. Arrested on January 14, 1986.

The defendant Zhao Hengdong was charged with embezzlement. On April 29, 1986, the Shenyang Municipal People's Procuratorate of Liaoning Province initiated a public prosecution with the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court. Upon review, the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court returned the case to the Shenyang Municipal People's Procuratorate for supplementary investigation due to insufficient evidence. On June 22 of the same year, the Shenyang Municipal People's Procuratorate again transferred the case to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court.

The indictment determined the following criminal facts of Zhao Hengdong:

From December 8, 1984, to March 20, 1985, the defendant Zhao Hengdong, taking advantage of his position in charge of the translation, publication, and sale of Chinese-language materials for PC microcomputers (hereinafter "PC Materials") by the Liaoning Provincial Computer Society, used contract means for "scientific and technological consulting and intellectual development" to divert payments totaling RMB 350,505 from 16 entities—including the Scientific Instrument Factory of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the Science and Technology Equipment Service Company of the Shenyang Branch of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Factory of the Shenyang Institute of Computing Technology—for the purchase of the Society's "PC Materials," into the Liaoning Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center and the Intellectual Development Center, respectively. Then, Zhao, taking advantage of his convenience in custody of the official seal, affixed the seal without authorization and imitated the signature of Zhang Zhenyu, Chairman of the Liaoning Provincial Computer Society, to withdraw consulting allowances and incentive fees totaling RMB 99,756.8 on ten separate occasions, appropriating them for himself.

During December 1984, the Liaoning Provincial Computer Society sold 15 microcomputers on behalf of the Fujian Wuyi Economic and Technological Development Company, receiving consignment proceeds of RMB 25,396. Subsequently, Zhao used the means of signing a "scientific and technological consulting" business contract to transfer the consignment fees to the Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center, then affixed the official seal and imitated Zhang Zhenyu's signature to withdraw consulting allowances and incentive fees totaling RMB 7,200 from the Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center on four separate occasions, appropriating them for himself.

Zhao Hengdong deposited the total embezzled sum of RMB 106,956.8 in his own name and his wife's name in seven savings offices across three districts, and withdrew interest of RMB 1,903.55.

After accepting the case, the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court designated special personnel to conduct a careful and thorough review of the criminal facts alleged against the defendant Zhao Hengdong in the procuratorate's indictment, lasting seven months. The court found:

In April 1984, the defendant Zhao Hengdong learned that China had introduced over 100,000 PC microcomputers from abroad, and the accompanying foreign-language materials (manuals) were limited and scattered, while a vast number of users eagerly desired a comprehensive and systematic set of Chinese-language materials. To meet user needs, Zhao Hengdong, in consultation with Society Chairman Zhang Zhenyu, decided to collect original PC microcomputer materials and, under the Society's name, organize a group of scientific and technical personnel proficient in both their specialty and foreign languages to translate the materials during their spare time. On June 14, 1984, Zhao Hengdong organized 22 translators, represented by Liu Ximing, and signed a translation agreement for "PC Materials" with them. The agreement specified translation requirements, submission deadlines, and royalty standards. The agreement did not specify how profits would be distributed. To address funding difficulties, Zhao Hengdong employed a method of pre-collecting payment from subscribers and sent out order forms for "PC Materials" to 28 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the central government. After the materials were translated, Zhao, in consultation with Zhang Zhenyu, printed 7,000 sets. During the printing process, using a method of printing and selling simultaneously, 1,805 sets of materials were directly sold. Concurrently, pre-orders for 1,185 sets were received from users. The Financial Office of the Shenyang Institute of Computing Technology, which managed the funds, received a total of RMB 346,996 in subscription payments from users. During this period, Society Chairman Zhang Zhenyu, preparing for a job transfer, discussed the distribution of royalties with Zhao Hengdong. Zhao proposed a distribution plan and withdrew RMB 279,889.08 from the Institute's Financial Office, which was used for: printing costs RMB 219,304.75, freight and miscellaneous expenses RMB 22,266.44, royalties RMB 26,362.50, and energy fees RMB 11,955.39. To supply all printed but unsold materials to users, Zhao Hengdong, together with Society Chairman Zhang Zhenyu, obtained the consent of the manager of the Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center, and on behalf of the Scientific and Technological Consulting Service Center of the Liaoning Provincial Computer Society, signed five scientific and technological consulting contracts with "PC Materials" users through the Liaoning Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center and Intellectual Development Center, transferring 5,195 sets of "PC Materials" (including the 1,185 pre-ordered sets) for a total contract value of RMB 360,505. In December 1985, Zhao Hengdong signed a scientific and technological consulting business contract with Fujian Wuyi Economic and Technological Development Company to assist in selling 15 PCs. The Wuyi Company paid a technical consulting service fee of RMB 25,395 as per the contract, which was transferred to the account of the Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center. From March to August 10, 1985, Zhao Hengdong, pursuant to the contract provisions allowing a 30% withdrawal for technical consulting fees and incentive fees, withdrew RMB 106,956.8 from the Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center and Intellectual Development Center. Due to the large amount withdrawn, the undetermined distribution plan, the incomplete overall work, unsettled accounts, and to prevent loss of the large sum, Zhao Hengdong deposited the money in his own name and his wife's name in ten savings offices within the city, meticulously recording the withdrawal and deposit dates and amounts in a ledger. On November 11, 1985, Zhao Hengdong withdrew RMB 60 in deposit interest and immediately re-deposited it. On November 2 of the same year, Zhao withdrew RMB 1,228.42 in deposit interest, which, together with the remaining RMB 75.13 from the previous interest re-deposit, was kept in a filing cabinet in his office. The day before his arrest, Zhao carried this money on his person intending to deposit it; it was seized after his arrest. The above accounts, audited by financial experts, matched perfectly without any discrepancy; Zhao Hengdong had not touched a cent.

Regarding the means of embezzlement alleged in the indictment, the facts were as follows:

Concerning the allegation that "the defendant, taking advantage of his convenience in custody of the official seal, affixed the seal without authorization": Investigation revealed that the Liaoning Provincial Computer Society had been established for only a short time. When Zhao organized the aforementioned scientific and technological consulting activities, the Society, besides its Chairman, had only him handling the specific work. He was also the Deputy Secretary-General and the person in charge of this project. Therefore, there was no such thing as "affixing the seal without authorization."

Concerning the allegation that "the defendant imitated the signature of Zhang Zhenyu, Chairman of the Provincial Computer Society, to withdraw funds without authorization": Investigation revealed that Zhang Zhenyu confirmed that the signature "Zhang Zhenyu" written by Zhao Hengdong was not an imitation but Zhao's habitual handwriting. A technical handwriting examination also negated imitation. The indictment's determination of imitation was inconsistent with the facts. Personnel Yu Xuehong, Guo Tingshu, and He Sujuan from the Liaoning Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center and Intellectual Development Center testified that when Zhao Hengdong withdrew funds, he had to sign his own name in the "handler" and "branch responsible person" columns. Yu Xuehong asked if the Society had other responsible persons. Zhao said there was Zhang Zhenyu. Yu then asked Zhao to sign Zhang Zhenyu's name. They also testified that Zhao's fund withdrawals complied with the contract terms, bore the official seal of the representing agency, and had complete procedures.

Concerning the allegation that Zhao Hengdong deposited funds under his own name and his wife Wang Rongfang's name: Investigation revealed that on the morning of late May 1985, Zhao Hengdong withdrew over RMB 51,000 from the Liaoning Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center. As it was near noon and the banks would close in the afternoon, considering the large amount requiring a seal for deposit, he hurriedly picked up his wife Wang Rongfang's personal seal from home and went to deposit the money. Wang Rongfang was unaware of this. As for depositing under his own name, Zhao Hengdong, as the organizer of this project, the Society's responsible person, and its sole staff member, depositing the consulting fees due to a few individuals in his personal name in the bank was a legitimate act.

In summary, the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court held:

1. Zhao Hengdong's withdrawal of 30% consulting fees according to regulations was lawful. Document No. (82) Ke Xie Fa Zi 024 issued by the China Association for Science and Technology and the Ministry of Finance on February 15, 1982, stated: "Scientific and technological consulting services are a new endeavor and an important task in promoting the Four Modernizations," "a form for the science and technology sector to become socialized," and "the necessary expenses and remuneration should gradually be borne by the employing or commissioning parties, adopting a contract system." The document also included "providing technical consultation for the introduction of foreign technology and equipment" within the "scope of scientific and technological consulting services." The 1985 "Work Tasks and Business Scope of the Liaoning Provincial Scientific and Technological Consulting Center" included "technical consulting services" and "translation of scientific and technological materials" within its business scope. Documents from the Shenyang Branch of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (No. (85) 57), the Liaoning Provincial Association for Science and Technology (No. (83) 41), and the Shenyang Municipal Party Committee and Municipal Government (No. (1985) 30) all stipulated that scientific and technical personnel participating in consulting projects could receive remuneration not exceeding 30% of the net income. Thus, Zhao Hengdong organizing personnel to translate and print "PC Materials" during their spare time, legally signing contracts, and transferring the materials for a fee, and withdrawing 30% consulting fees therefrom was lawful.

2. Zhao Hengdong subjectively lacked the intent to embezzle over RMB 100,000. Zhao's opinions on handling the profits were recorded in his work diary and work summaries: "This sum of money is large and difficult to handle; the only option is to save it, and handle it at the end of the year based on the situation. If necessary, give some to the Institute, and some to the Provincial Association for Science and Technology, as rewards for comrades who have contributed to the work. How much I personally receive will be decided by the unit." "My personal opinion is to give the RMB 100,000 to the Institute, which can distribute it according to consulting regulations to those involved in this work. The remaining funds after the commission could buy a car, with ownership belonging to the Institute and usage rights for the Society." Zhao Hengdong reported these opinions to leading comrades including Lan Guixing (Deputy Director of the Shenyang Institute of Computing Technology), Liu Guangdi, and Zhang Zhenyu. Zhao also expressed these opinions to many people at different times and places. These facts were all corroborated.

3. Objectively, Zhao Hengdong did not engage in embezzlement. Although Zhao deposited the funds in his and his wife's names, he kept clear records in the cash ledger he established. The signing of consulting contracts was conducted openly, and the withdrawal of 30% consulting fees in accordance with relevant regulations was well-known. Although Zhao concurrently held the position of Deputy Secretary-General of the Computer Society, he was still an employee of the Institute of Computing Technology. Therefore, the relevant regulations of the Institute of Computing Technology constrained and limited how Zhao handled these funds. Zhao organized the translation and printing of the "PC Materials," with all accounts managed by the Institute's Finance Office, and income and expenses were subject to the Institute's supervision.

4. The consulting fees withdrawn by Zhao Hengdong were remuneration earned by scientific and technical personnel through spare-time work. Under China's Criminal Law, the direct object of the crime of embezzlement must be public property; without infringing upon public property, the crime of embezzlement is not constituted. Regarding the income obtained by Zhao organizing over 20 scientific and technical personnel to translate "PC Materials" during their spare time, according to the central government's decision on the reform of the science and technology system, which stipulated that "scientific and technical personnel may, on the premise of completing their regular duties and not infringing upon the unit's technical rights and economic interests, engage in spare-time technical work and consulting services, with the income belonging to themselves," the withdrawal of 30% consulting fees was entirely reasonable and proper.

Accordingly, the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court confirmed that Zhao Hengdong's conduct did not violate the Criminal Law and did not constitute the crime of embezzlement. Pursuant to Article 10 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and Item (1) of Article 11 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the defendant Zhao Hengdong was declared acquitted and released.
